name: Sails Over the Edge: The Great Voyages of Discovery
description: Treasure fleets, caravels and survey ships: the voyages that linked every ocean and every continent, and what they cost the people they met.

checkpoints.name: Before the caravels
checkpoints.note: Polynesian navigators crossed the Pacific in canoes using stars and swells, and about the year 1000 Leif Erikson's Norse sailors reached North America. Long ocean voyages were old before Europeans took to them.

checkpoints.name: Treasure fleets
checkpoints.note: The Ming fleets of Zheng He cross the Indian Ocean, while Portuguese ships, backed by Prince Henry the Navigator, creep down the African coast until Dias rounds its southern tip. Two different empires test what the ocean can offer.

checkpoints.name: Round the world
checkpoints.note: Columbus reaches the Caribbean, da Gama reaches India and Magellan's fleet closes the circle. Cartier, Drake, Hudson and Tasman follow. The seas become a single network, with lasting harm to the peoples of the lands reached.

checkpoints.name: The age of survey
checkpoints.note: Navies send scientists to chart coasts, watch the sky and gather plants and animals. Cook and the Beagle's voyage change maps, and Darwin's ideas, and inland parties follow the rivers.

checkpoints.name: The last blank spaces
checkpoints.note: Explorers fill in the final gaps on land and in the sea. Expeditions probe the deep ocean and the Australian interior, and a raft crosses the Pacific to test a theory.
